editorial.headline: Plastic Material Recovery With a Clear Bali Registration Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 38302 covers the recovery of used plastic into secondary raw material, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 38302 is the activity of recovering material from used plastic goods. In plain English, it is not general trading, product retail, or a broad waste-management label; the record defines a narrower industrial activity: processing used plastic items into secondary raw material. Its practical centre is the sorting of plastic and the processing of plastic waste into granules, the intermediary material that can return discarded plastic into a production chain.

That scope matters because this code is about transformation, not merely collection. The activity described in the record begins with plastic as waste or used goods and ends with a secondary raw material. For founders, the clean reading is therefore a plastic recovery operation whose core work is sorting and granulation. The Indonesian title, *Pemulihan Material Barang Plastik*, carries the same sense: plastic material recovery, with the emphasis on recovering usable material from goods that have already left their first life.

The code is open across the full scale range shown in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity is not framed only for large industrial operators; it can be registered at every listed business scale, from micro through large. Nationally, the PMA position is also straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the cited source. In ordinary investor language, the national rule in this record allows a fully foreign-owned PMA structure for this activity.

The Bali picture is unusually clean as well. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest reading is therefore not a hidden Bali cap or a local-percentage condition; the slim record contains none. For this code, the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling stands, and the Bali field says the activity is not blocked by the moratorium.
